## Overview

When K2 Horizon output has no end-of-thinking token and no tool calls (for example cut off by `max_tokens`), non-streaming returns the thinking text as `content`, while streaming returns it as `reasoning`. This PR makes non-streaming return it as `reasoning`, like streaming and like `DeepSeekR1ReasoningParser`.

## Claims

- A K2 Horizon response cut off during thinking now has the text in `reasoning` and `content: null`, in both streaming and non-streaming mode.
- Outputs with `</ifm|think>` (or the `medium`/`low` end tokens) or with `<ifm|tool_calls>` parse exactly as before.

## Validation

New unit test `test_unfinished_reasoning_matches_streaming` runs the same output through both modes and checks they agree.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py
python -m pytest -q tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Before (test only) | `1 failed, 15 passed`: `assert ('', 'still planning') == ('still planning', None)` |
| After | `16 passed`; with the K2 Horizon tool parser tests, `42 passed` |

End-to-end check with K2 Horizon, `--reasoning-parser k2_horizon`, a prompt that needs long thinking and a small `max_tokens` (for example 64):

Parser check with the real K2 Horizon tokenizer (`tokenizer.json` from `IFM/K2-Horizon-7B`, 250,624 tokens including `<ifm|think>` and `</ifm|think>`). The output stops before `</ifm|think>`, as it does when `max_tokens` runs out, and goes through `run_reasoning_extraction`, streamed one decoded token at a time:

Output: `<ifm|think>Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi`

| Mode | `main` (`reasoning` / `content`) | This PR (`reasoning` / `content`) |
|---|---|---|
| non-streaming | `""` / `"Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"` | `"Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"` / `null` |
| streaming | `"Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"` / `null` | `"Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"` / `null` |

On `main` the same truncated output lands in `content` or in `reasoning` depending only on whether the client streams. With this PR both modes agree.

Not run end to end on a GPU yet. The check above uses the model's real tokenizer and special tokens, and the parser has no other inputs on this path.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
    from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast
    from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
    from vllm.reasoning import ReasoningParserManager
    from tests.reasoning.utils import run_reasoning_extraction

    tok = PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_file=hf_hub_download("IFM/K2-Horizon-7B", "tokenizer.json"))
    req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="IFM/K2-Horizon-7B", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Plan a trip to Hanoi"}], max_tokens=12)
    out = "<ifm|think>Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"
    pieces = [tok.decode([i]) for i in tok.encode(out, add_special_tokens=False)]
    for streaming in (False, True):
        parser = ReasoningParserManager.get_reasoning_parser("k2_horizon")(tok)
        print(streaming, run_reasoning_extraction(parser, pieces, req, streaming=streaming))

</details>

## Details

Root cause: the last line of `_split_model_output` was `return "", output or None`. The streaming path in the same class buffers that text as reasoning, `extract_content_ids` returns no content ids, and there is no streaming fallback that moves it to content. K2 Horizon has no "thinking off" effort (`reasoning_effort` must be `high`, `medium` or `low`), so text before any boundary is always thinking. The line is now `return output, None`.

Not a duplicate: I searched PRs for "k2 horizon" and open PRs for unfinished or non-streaming reasoning. #59627 changes how the implicit reasoning end reaches structured output and does not touch this function. #57768 adds regex timeouts to the K2 Horizon tool parser. The other open PRs about truncated reasoning are for Kimi K3. No issue reports this bug.

Co-author: Claude.

---

This is a Bytebell PR verification bot.
I have found an issue: [Full report here](https://production.mcp.bytebell.ai/vllm-project/vllm/main/60969)

## Findings — 2 in 2 files

### [`vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py)

#### major · breaks consumer · [line 62](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L62)

Content is now None for truncated output; K2HorizonToolParser._content_or_none calls content.strip(), so a serving path that forwards this content makes the tool parser raise.

Evidence:

- change [`vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py` 62](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L62) — The fallback now returns reasoning=output, content=None, where base returned the text as content.
- base [`vllm/tool_parsers/k2_horizon_tool_parser.py` 119-129](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/tool_parsers/k2_horizon_tool_parser.py#L119-L129) — _content_or_none does content.strip() and _no_tool_calls passes it straight through, so None raises AttributeError.
- base [`vllm/tool_parsers/k2_horizon_tool_parser.py` 289-300](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/tool_parsers/k2_horizon_tool_parser.py#L289-L300) — extract_tool_calls types its argument as str and routes a text with no <ifm|tool_calls> through _no_tool_calls(model_output).

### [`tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py)

#### minor · tests · [lines 134–146](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L134-L146)

Docstring asserts both modes agree for pre-boundary truncation, but streaming withholds a partial-tag tail that nothing ever flushes, so such outputs still disagree; untested.

Evidence:

- change [`tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py` 133-146](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L133-L146) — The added test claims mode parity for 'output cut off before any boundary', yet its streaming call sends the entire text in one delta and never reaches end-of-stream, so the withheld-tail case is never exercised.
- base [`vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py` 144-152](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L144-L152) — In the no-boundary branch the streaming path computes partial_tag_overlap and emits only the sendable prefix, keeping the rest in _stream_buffer; the non-streaming return the patch adds has no such withholding.
- base [`vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` 47-57](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py#L47-L57) — partial_tag_overlap returns up to len(tag)-1, so the final characters of a truncated output can be held back indefinitely and are never emitted as reasoning.
- base [`vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py` 801-821](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py#L801-L821) — The composed parser's only end-of-stream flush promotes withheld text through get_streaming_fallback_content, which K2HorizonReasoningParser does not define, so a stream cut mid-tail loses text non-streaming now returns.

Sure @chaunceyjiang. Real run on an RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB, vLLM `0.1.dev22857+g2d18b3427` (this branch). Same server and request on `main` and on this PR; only `vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py` differs between the two runs.

Server:

    vllm serve IFM/K2-Horizon-7B --reasoning-parser k2_horizon --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enforce-eager --port 8000 --trust-remote-code

(FP8 only so the 9B model fits in 16 GB.)

Request (`"stream": true` for the streaming rows):

    curl localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
      "model": "IFM/K2-Horizon-7B",
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Plan a 3-day trip to Hanoi for a family with two kids."}],
      "max_tokens": 32, "temperature": 0, "seed": 0, "stream": false}'

The chat template ends the prompt with `<ifm|think>\n`, so the output starts inside thinking. With `max_tokens: 32` it stops before `</ifm|think>` (`finish_reason: "length"` in all four runs). This is the usual case of a response cut off by the token limit.

Output text in all four runs: `The user just typed a blank line? The conversation: system says "You are K2...". The user message is empty (just a newline). The user likely`

| | `reasoning` | `content` |
|---|---|---|
| `main`, stream=false | `""` | the text above |
| `main`, stream=true | the text above | `null` |
| this PR, stream=false | the text above | `null` |
| this PR, stream=true | the text above | `null` |

On `main` the same cut-off thinking comes back as `content` without streaming and as `reasoning` with streaming. With this PR both modes return it as `reasoning`, which matches `DeepSeekR1ReasoningParser` when the end token is missing.

Side note, unrelated to this PR: the model says the user message is empty, and `prompt_tokens` is 10. vLLM detects this template's content format as `openai`, and the template renders only string `content`, so the question is dropped from the prompt. The parser only sees the output text, so the split above does not depend on it.

Output text in all four runs: `The user just typed a blank line? The conversation: system says "You are K2...". The user message is empty (just a newline). The user likely`

| | `reasoning` | `content` |
|---|---|---|
| `main`, stream=false | `""` | the text above |
| `main`, stream=true | the text above | `null` |
| this PR, stream=false | the text above | `null` |
| this PR, stream=true | the text above | `null` |

On `main` the same cut-off thinking comes back as `content` without streaming and as `reasoning` with streaming. With this PR both modes return it as `reasoning`, which matches `DeepSeekR1ReasoningParser` when the end token is missing.

Side note, unrelated to this PR: the model says the user message is empty, and `prompt_tokens` is 10. vLLM detects this template's content format as `openai`, and the template renders only string `content`, so the question is dropped from the prompt. The parser only sees the output text, so the split above does not depend on it.

## Findings — 2 in 2 files

### [`vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py)

#### major · breaks consumer · [line 62](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L62)

Content is now None for truncated output; K2HorizonToolParser._content_or_none calls content.strip(), so a serving path that forwards this content makes the tool parser raise.

Evidence:

- change [`vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py` 62](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L62) — The fallback now returns reasoning=output, content=None, where base returned the text as content.
- base [`vllm/tool_parsers/k2_horizon_tool_parser.py` 119-129](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/tool_parsers/k2_horizon_tool_parser.py#L119-L129) — _content_or_none does content.strip() and _no_tool_calls passes it straight through, so None raises AttributeError.
- base [`vllm/tool_parsers/k2_horizon_tool_parser.py` 289-300](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/tool_parsers/k2_horizon_tool_parser.py#L289-L300) — extract_tool_calls types its argument as str and routes a text with no <ifm|tool_calls> through _no_tool_calls(model_output).

### [`tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py)

#### minor · tests · [lines 134–146](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L134-L146)

Docstring asserts both modes agree for pre-boundary truncation, but streaming withholds a partial-tag tail that nothing ever flushes, so such outputs still disagree; untested.

Evidence:

- change [`tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py` 133-146](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0fb8ba3fbfd9f35432fc6fc80ab1e779c15c679/tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L133-L146) — The added test claims mode parity for 'output cut off before any boundary', yet its streaming call sends the entire text in one delta and never reaches end-of-stream, so the withheld-tail case is never exercised.
- base [`vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py` 144-152](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/reasoning/k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py#L144-L152) — In the no-boundary branch the streaming path computes partial_tag_overlap and emits only the sendable prefix, keeping the rest in _stream_buffer; the non-streaming return the patch adds has no such withholding.
- base [`vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` 47-57](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py#L47-L57) — partial_tag_overlap returns up to len(tag)-1, so the final characters of a truncated output can be held back indefinitely and are never emitted as reasoning.
- base [`vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py` 801-821](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8674a794c788d4c7dac10c6f7ddfdae677588d18/vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py#L801-L821) — The composed parser's only end-of-stream flush promotes withheld text through get_streaming_fallback_content, which K2HorizonReasoningParser does not define, so a stream cut mid-tail loses text non-streaming now returns.

Thanks for the check. On the first point: in the serving path the tool parser never receives None. `_extract_tool_calls` passes `content if content is not None else ""` for auto tool choice and `content or ""` for tool_choice="none" (vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py lines 394 and 447). Returning `(output, None)` when the end token is missing is also what `BaseThinkingReasoningParser.extract_reasoning` already does (vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py lines 170-171), so this matches the base contract.

On the second point: you are right that streaming holds back a partial `</ifm|think>` tail and never flushes it. That behavior exists on main and this PR does not change the streaming path, so I kept it out of scope. The test covers output with no end tag at all; I can narrow the docstring to say that if reviewers prefer.

Shall I double verify before publishing?
Or any other ask you would like me to do ? @hpdkhoa
